fresh-sarc.ipynb.source:
# pass patient name to R env
%R -i pat_list

%%R

# Load data set using read function for filtered count matrix produced by CellBender v2.1.
# From CellBender docs: "'filtered' means that this file contains only the droplets which were
# determined to have a > 50% posterior probability of containing cells."
object.list <- lapply(pat_list, function (x) Read10X_h5(paste0("../cellbender/",pat,"/",pat,'_filtered.h5'), 
                       use.names = TRUE, unique.features = TRUE)
)

%%R

# Initialize the Seurat object with the raw (non-normalized) data
# Project name is the patient name
# Include features dectected in at least 1 cell
# Include cells with at least 1 detected feature
seu_raw.list <- lapply(X = seq_along(object.list), FUN = function(i) {
    x <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = object.list[[i]], project = pat_list[[i]], min.cells = 1, min.features = 1)  
})

# seu_raw.list <- lapply(pat_list, function (x) readRDS(paste0('data/', x, '/data_', x, '_cb_raw.rds')))

%%R
# Annotate patient info
for(i in 1:length(seu_raw.list)) {
    seu_raw.list[[i]][['patient']] <- pat_list[[i]]
}
# seu_raw[['organ']] <- 'Lung'
# seu_raw[['group']] <- substr(pat, 4, 6)
# seu_raw[['ID']] <- substr(pat, 1, 3)

# read counts matrix file written by writeMM above

counts_list = []
for pat in pat_list:
    counts_matrix = scipy.io.mmread(''.join(['data/', pat, '/matrix_', pat, '_raw.mtx'])).T.tocsc()

    # run scrublet using expected doublet rate
    scrub = scr.Scrublet(counts_matrix, expected_doublet_rate=doublet_rate)
    doublet_scores, predicted_doublets = scrub.scrub_doublets(min_counts=1, min_cells=1,
                                                              min_gene_variability_pctl=50,
                                                              n_prin_comps=20)
    print(doublet_scores, predicted_doublets)
    
    
    with open(''.join(['data/', pat, '/doublets_', pat, '_raw.txt']),'w') as outFI:
        outFI.write('predicted_doublets\tdoublet_scores\n')
        for j in range(len(predicted_doublets)):
            outFI.write(str(predicted_doublets[j]).upper()+'\t'+str(doublet_scores[j])+'\n')

%%R
for(i in 1:length(seu.list)) {
    pat <- pat_list[[i]]
    print(paste0("[", pat, "] num cells: ", length(Cells(seu.list[[i]]))))

    # Save object
    saveRDS(seu.list[[i]], file = paste0('data/', pat, '/data_', pat, '_genes_', minFeature, '_UMI_', minCount, '.rds'))
    
#     counts_matrix = GetAssayData(seu.list[[i]], slot="counts")
#     saveRDS(round(counts_matrix, digits=3), paste0('data/', pat, '/data_', pat, '_genes_', minFeature, '_UMI_', minCount, '_counts_mtx.rds'))
}

title: Profiling of Sarcomas from Archival Tissues [lp-WGS]
summary: We performed single nuclei RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) with matched T cell receptor sequencing (TCR-seq), and pool matched low pass whole genome sequencing (WGS) of eight specimens from six patients, encompassing four undifferentiated polymorphic sarcomas (UPS)  and four intimal sarcomas (INS), and paired specimens from two patients (one UPS and INS each) treated with immune checkpoint blockade (ICB).
overall_design: Pool matched lp-WGS was performed in addtion to single-nuclei RNA which involved 75,716 cell transcriptomes and  an average of 9465 cell transcriptomes per specimen. Together, this data served to improve the identification of the malignant and non-malignant cell compartments within the 8 collected samples of frozen sarcoma tissue.
Submitter states that missing raw data are being made available for controlled access in dbGaP.
